title: Mooney M20J 201 — Emergency Procedures
description: Emergency procedures for the Mooney M20J 201 with Lycoming IO-360 fuel-injected engine, constant-speed propeller, and electric retractable tricycle gear. Memory items are marked. The IO-360 is fuel-injected — carburetor icing is not applicable, but induction system blockage and vapor lock at high density altitude are possible concerns; a note is included. Gear emergencies include electric gear failure and manual extension using the emergency gear extension system. All airspeeds and numeric limits must come from the specific aircraft POH. Not a substitute for recurrent emergency training.

source.notes: No manufacturer document consulted. Written from general familiarity with the type.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities, or other numerical limitations — all must come from the specific aircraft POH.
Emergency gear extension procedure varies by model year and modification. Verify the exact procedure for this specific airframe's gear system before flight.
Equipment varies across M20J airframes. Verify every item against the specific aircraft and its POH before use.

sections.title: Engine Failure on Takeoff — Before or At Liftoff
sections.condition: Engine power loss during the takeoff roll or at the moment of liftoff

items.text: Throttle
Brakes — apply firmly to stop within remaining runway
Mixture
Ignition switch
Master switch
Fuel selector
Do not attempt to remain airborne if the engine fails at or near liftoff. The M20J does not climb on partial power from low speed. Land on available runway or surface ahead.
If briefly airborne — land straight ahead on remaining runway or overrun; do not turn back
Occupants

sections.title: Engine Failure After Takeoff — Airborne, Low Altitude
sections.condition: Engine failure after liftoff with insufficient altitude for return to airport

items.text: Airspeed — establish best glide immediately
Landing area — select nearest suitable surface ahead within glide; do not attempt to return to runway below safe altitude
Throttle
items.response: FULL — brief restart attempt if altitude permits

items.text: Fuel selector
Mixture
Ignition switch
items.response: BOTH — confirm ON; try START if engine has stopped

items.text: If engine does not restart — secure and commit to forced landing
Gear — extend only when landing is assured on the chosen surface; if surface is marginal, consider leaving gear retracted
items.response: DOWN WHEN COMMITTED; OR GEAR UP FOR ROUGH TERRAIN

sections.title: Engine Failure in Flight
sections.condition: Sudden loss of engine power at cruise altitude with time to troubleshoot

items.text: Airspeed — establish best glide
Landing area — identify a reachable field or airport within glide range
Fuel selector
items.response: BOTH — or switch to fuller tank

items.text: Mixture
Throttle
Ignition switch
items.response: BOTH — confirm ON; cycle START if engine is not turning

items.text: Fuel pump (boost pump)
items.response: ON — check fuel pressure; look for vapor lock

items.text: Primer
Mayday call — squawk 7700; declare on 121.5 MHz or ATC frequency
If restart unsuccessful — secure engine and continue to forced landing
Mixture
Fuel selector
Throttle
items.response: FULL OPEN — to exhaust any residual fuel in the induction system

items.text: Master switch
Cabin heat and vents from engine compartment
items.response: CLOSED — prevent flame and fumes from entering cabin

items.text: Airspeed — increase to attempt to extinguish flame with slipstream; do not exceed Vne
If fire persists — initiate emergency descent toward forced landing area
Mayday — declare on 121.5 or ATC frequency; squawk 7700
Prepare for forced landing — follow Forced Landing checklist as able

sections.title: Engine Fire on Ground — During or After Start

items.text: Throttle — advance and keep cranking with starter to draw fire back into engine
items.detail: On a fuel-injected engine, if the fire is in the induction system, continuing to crank and advance throttle may pull the burning fuel back through. If fire is external to the engine, shut down immediately.

items.text: Mixture
Ignition switch
Fuel selector
Master switch
Evacuate aircraft — all occupants exit immediately and move upwind
Fire extinguisher — direct at base of flame; avoid directing into induction inlet if fire is out
Emergency services

sections.title: Electrical Fire or Smoke in Cockpit

items.text: Master switch
Avionics master
Cabin vents — open to flush smoke; avoid fanning the source
All electrical switches — off individually; identify the circuit causing the smoke before restoring power
Fire extinguisher — if flame visible, use extinguisher; CO2 or halon preferred for electrical
items.response: DISCHARGE AT SOURCE IF FLAME VISIBLE

items.text: Circuit breakers — inspect; do not reset a breaker that has popped due to suspected overload without identifying the cause
items.response: DO NOT RESET HOT BREAKERS BLINDLY

items.text: Land as soon as practicable — electrical fires can re-ignite and avionics may be unavailable
Essential avionics — restore one item at a time to navigate if master is safe to restore
Power — reduce to minimum required to maintain safe flight
Land as soon as possible — do not delay; continued operation with low or zero oil pressure risks engine seizure
Oil temperature — monitor; rising temp with low pressure confirms oil loss
Mixture
items.response: FULL RICH — to help cool the engine

items.text: Nearest airport — identify and begin approach without delay
Mayday — declare if engine condition is deteriorating
If engine begins to run rough or seize — shut down and follow Forced Landing checklist

sections.phase_label: Induction System Blockage / Fuel System Malfunction
sections.title: Induction System Blockage or Fuel System Malfunction
sections.condition: Engine roughness, power loss, or stumble not resolved by mixture adjustment; not carburetor ice (IO-360 is fuel-injected)

items.text: The Lycoming IO-360 is fuel-injected and does not have a carburetor. Carburetor icing is not applicable. However, induction icing, vapor lock, or fuel system contamination can cause similar symptoms.
Alternate air control (alternate induction air) — open to bypass blocked air filter
Fuel selector
items.response: BOTH — or switch to fuller tank

items.text: Mixture
Fuel pump (boost pump)
items.response: ON — monitor fuel flow for vapor lock

items.text: Engine instruments — monitor for improvement; if power does not recover, prepare for forced landing
If no improvement — declare emergency and land as soon as possible
Airspeed — establish and maintain best glide immediately
Landing area — select the best available field within glide range; consider wind, slope, surface, and obstacles
Mayday — squawk 7700; transmit position, altitude, and intentions on 121.5 MHz
Restart attempt — fuel selector BOTH, mixture RICH, ignition BOTH, boost pump ON, throttle to full momentarily
items.response: ATTEMPT IF ALTITUDE AND TIME PERMIT

items.text: If restart fails: mixture — idle cutoff
Fuel selector
Ignition switch
Master switch — leave on long enough to lower gear; then OFF before touchdown unless radio needed
items.response: ON FOR GEAR; OFF BEFORE TOUCHDOWN

items.text: Landing gear — extend when landing is certain on the chosen field; if surface is rough or soft, consider gear-up landing to reduce injury risk
items.response: DOWN IF SURFACE SUITABLE; UP IF NOT
items.detail: A gear-up landing on grass or soft ground is often survivable with less occupant injury than a gear-collapse on rough terrain. The POH or POH emergency section should be consulted during training for this decision.

items.text: Flaps — extend to increase drag and reduce approach speed when field is assured
Seat belts and shoulder harnesses — all occupants
Doors — unlatch before touchdown to prevent jamming
Occupants — brief to brace; remove glasses; loosen any items that could become projectiles

sections.title: Landing Gear Unsafe Indication
sections.condition: One or more gear indicator lights not showing green on approach, or red unsafe light illuminated

items.text: Airspeed — maintain safe approach speed; do not rush; remain at altitude to troubleshoot
Gear handle — confirm in the DOWN position
Gear circuit breaker — check; reset once if tripped
Cycle gear — raise and re-select down; allow time for full extension and lock
Gear warning horn — verify it sounds with throttle at idle (confirms unsafe condition is real, not a bulb failure)
If gear will not extend normally — proceed to Emergency Gear Extension checklist
ATC — advise of gear situation; request emergency services to stand by

sections.title: Emergency Gear Extension
sections.condition: Normal electric gear system has failed to extend the landing gear

items.text: Emergency gear extension procedures vary between M20J model years and by modification. The following represents a typical procedure. Verify the exact steps for this specific aircraft in its POH before flight.
Airspeed — reduce to gear extension speed or below (Vlo) per POH
Gear handle — DOWN
Gear circuit breaker — check and reset if popped
Manual gear extension handle or release — locate and actuate per POH procedure to release hydraulic pressure or mechanical uplock
items.detail: The M20J uses an electrically-driven hydraulic gear system on most variants. Emergency extension typically involves releasing hydraulic pressure via a manual valve, allowing gravity and airflow to extend and lock the gear. Consult the specific aircraft POH and practice the procedure on the ground.

items.text: Allow time for gear to fall and lock under gravity and airstream
Gear position indicators — verify three green
If only partial green — do not cycle; land gently with known gear configuration; alert fire/rescue
items.response: LAND WITH AVAILABLE CONFIGURATION; FIRE RESCUE ON STANDBY

items.text: Approach and landing — fly a normal stabilized approach; do not extend flaps if doing so would reduce gear-locking airflow on some configurations (verify per POH)
